data.name: Ezekan
data.long_meaning: Ezekiel was a prophet of God in the Old Testament, whose name means 'God will strengthen'. He was a key figure in the Babylonian exile, and his visions of the future are central to the book of Ezekiel. Despite the challenges and suffering of exile, Ezekiel's faith remained steadfast, and he was a symbol of God's unwavering love and care for his people.

historical_references.reference: Ezekiel the monk (480-530 AD) was a monk of the Laura of Sinai. He is best known for his ascetic practices and his writings, which include descriptions of the visions he received during periods of contemplation. The visions were later compiled into the 'Apocryphal Book of Ezekiel'.

Ezekiel of Jerusalem (circa 1522-1572 AD) was a Greek Orthodox monk and theologian. He is best remembered for his opposition to the Union of Churches, which aimed to unite the Eastern and Western Churches. Ezekiel wrote extensively on the subject, and his works continue to be studied by scholars of Orthodox theology.

Additionally, it is used in literature and literature analysis for its historical and cultural significance.
